merger_description:
Australian Rugby League Commission Limited (**ARLC**) proposes to acquire 100% of the freehold land interest, buildings, licenses and business assets (both tangible and intangible) of the Novotel Sydney International Airport in Wolli Creek, New South Wales (the **Novotel**) from entities of Charter Hall, as described in the transaction documents provided as part of the application (the **Acquisition**).

The Novotel, located at 22 Levey Street, Wolli Creek, New South Wales, offers hotel accommodation services (and ancillary services related to the operation of a hotel).

ARLC is the peak administrative body of the sport of rugby league in Australia and as part of its broader investment strategy owns and operates accommodation and hospitality venues across New South Wales and Queensland.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between ARLC and the Novotel
in the supply of short-term accommodation in the Sydney
Airport area, and only a very small overlap in Sydney more
broadly
b. there are alternative suppliers of short-term accommodation
in the Sydney Airport area and in Sydney more broadly.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
